subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & performance SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & performance SLOs

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sam — good conversation. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we schedule the run.

Recap / what I heard you ask for:
- Target latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end <= 150ms for typical UI prompts (512-token context). If possible you indicated preference for p95 <= 100ms but we should treat 150ms as the minimum acceptable.
- Streaming requirements: first-byte <= 120ms, steady-state per-token <= 50ms; support for chunked streaming (you stream partial results to clients).
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained throughput target ~120 req/s for the mixed prompt set; concurrency target of 64 concurrent sessions.
- Reproducibility & methodology: you want a runnable harness + prompt set + measurement definitions so you can re-run locally and validate results. You specifically asked about cold vs warm cache measurements, warm-up runs, hardware, and deterministic seeds.

What we will deliver for the first benchmark:
1) Benchmark harness (attached stub: benchmark-harness-v1.tar.gz) — runnable script + Dockerfile that executes the prompt set across configured concurrency levels and collects latency distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99), per-token streaming latencies, and throughput. Includes options for cold-warm cache toggles and controlled warmup iterations.
2) Prompt set (attached: edgefin-prompt-set-v2.csv) — mix of short UI prompts, long-context sequences, and multi-step tool-calling prompts you mentioned.
3) Reproducible runbook (repro-runbook.md) — measurement definitions, recommended hardware (A100 80GB), exact kernel/config flags we used, and instructions to reproduce.
4) Test plan — SE-led run on Redwood Dedicated node, we will capture raw logs and upload results to S3 and share a Drive link.

Open questions / clarifications for you:
- Is the 512-token context representative for most of your traffic, or should we add a 1024-token bucket for a small % of requests?
- For streaming, do you measure SLOs from client perceived first-byte or token-complete time? We assumed first-byte + per-token steady-state.
- Any requirement around model variants (e.g., must be our full fp16 variant vs quantized 4-bit)? If you have a strict accuracy baseline we should pin the model.

Next steps (proposed):
- SE run window: suggest two options the week of July 2 or July 6 — pick one and we’ll reserve Dedicated capacity.
- I’ll drop the harness + prompt set in Drive and schedule a short run with Dev to validate config.

Attachments: edgefin-prompt-set-v2.csv, benchmark-harness-v1.tar.gz, repro-runbook.md

If that looks right, reply with preferred test window and the 1–2 model variants you want us to exercise first.

Best,

Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & performance SLOs

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures everything. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: our preference is p95 <= 100ms for the majority of UI requests, but we can accept p95 <= 150ms as an initial bar. If you can show a plan to get to 100ms (kernel/runtime/config tuning, batching profiles) that will help our internal stakeholders.

2) Context distribution: ~85% of requests are <= 512 tokens, ~12% are between 512-1024, and ~3% are >1024. Please include a small 1024 bucket so results reflect tail behavior.

3) Cold vs warm: we want both. Cold-start behavior is important for bursty workloads; please include controlled cold-cache runs (restart runtime, zero warmup) and warm-cache runs (simulate steady-state). Define warmup iterations in the runbook and include both p50/p90/p95/p99 for each scenario.

4) Hardware: we are primarily interested in results on A100 80GB (our planned Dedicated target) but would also like a run on a cheaper GPU class to understand cost tradeoffs (e.g., A10 or T4). If Redwood can provide both, that would be ideal.

5) Model variants: we want to exercise both the full fp16 variant and a 4-bit quantized variant. Accuracy regressions must be measured — please include automated evals (exact-match / token-level BLEU or your chosen metric) in the harness.

One more ask: can you make the harness deterministic (fixed RNG seed, pinned kernels), and provide the exact command line/invocation you used for each measurement so we can re-run?

I’m available to confirm test windows next week. If you need anything from our infra team (VPN, IP allowlist for Dedicated node access), let me know and I’ll loop them in.

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Product Engineering Manager | EdgeFin Solutions
sam.jenkins@edgefin.com

Thanks Marissa/Sam. Proposed plan and next steps: 

1) Plan: Dev (cc’d) will run the harness in our Dedicated staging cluster. We will run the following matrix: 
- Model variants: fp16 (baseline), 4-bit quantized (cost-savings).
- Context buckets: <=512, 512-1024, >1024 (small sample).
- Cache modes: cold (restart between runs), warm (steady-state after N warmup iterations).
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32, 64.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), first-byte streaming latency, per-token steady-state latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory/KV cache hit rates.

2) Reproducibility: Dev will publish the exact invocation and Docker image tag we used; we will attach seeds and kernel flags. The runbook will include the warmup iteration count (default 250 requests) and a suggested random-seed for deterministic runs.

3) Environment: We can run on A100 80GB for the baseline. We can also schedule an A10 run but it will be best-effort for capacity — if EdgeFin needs guaranteed A10 results we should lock capacity ahead of time.

4) Windows: propose two options — Jul 2, 2026 UTC 14:00-18:00 (preferred) or Jul 6, 2026 UTC 08:00-12:00. Please confirm preferred window and whether EdgeFin will provide an IP allowlist for Dedicated access.

5) Deliverables after run: raw logs on s3, a summarized report (CSV + PDF), and the reproducible runbook (repro-runbook.md) plus the harness. We’ll keep results in the Drive folder and link back to the HubSpot deal.
